data.name: Bocce Beach
data.detailed_description:
Step into the tropical paradise of Bocce Beach and play an immersive bocce ball game in VR!

You can naturally toss bocce balls on the beach with fun special effects and real-time sports commentary. Whether you want to play against the computer or compete with others for the Bocce Beach rankings, you’re guaranteed to have a blast!

The game supports both HTC Vive and Oculus Rift with touch controllers (360 tracking required).

reviews.review:
[quote][b]Note: Dead PvP game[/b]

This game contains no meaningful single player content.  There's no viably populated servers/active player population.  This game cannot be played as intended.[/quote]

"Bocce Beach" comes across as, well, a low key asset flip/kitbash.  The most likely explanation for this is when someone who isn't a professional game developer tries to shortcut the process by using a pile of pre-made assets. Without the talent to actually design a game, they just push this kind of junk as fast as they can onto Steam Direct, resulting in a product that doesn't hold much at all in terms of quality or interest.

It's VR only and barely works, with a few primitive plagiarized assets, a barely functioning Bocce simulation with some of the jankiest physics ever to insult gaming, and a bunch of completely fake positive reviews intended to mislead and scam you into buying garbage. 

Funly, LLC/My Way Games have shown a repeat pattern of unethically dumping other people's work onto Steam as a cheap, nasty cash grab. Here's some examples so you can see for yourself:

[list]
[*] "[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1050810]The Hunt in the Forest[/url]" = [url=https://assetstore.unity.com/packages/templates/systems/advanced-sniper-starter-kit-7593]Advanced Sniper Starter Kit[/url]
[*] "[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1020600]Extreme Truck Simulator[/url]" = [url=https://www.sellmyapp.com/downloads/crazy-cargo-truck-driver-2022/]Crazy Cargo Truck Driver[/url]
[*] "[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1058980]Dinosaur Bone Digging[/url]" = [url=https://www.sellanycode.com/item/515/dinosaur-bone-digging-games]Dinosaur Bone Digging Games[/url]
[*] "[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/628580]Miniballist[/url]" = [url=https://assetstore.unity.com/packages/templates/packs/endless-turns-63501]Endless Turns[/url]
[*] "[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1054930]Mine the Gold[/url]" = [url=https://unityassets4free.com/goldmine/]Gold Miner Century[/url]
[*] "[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1034160]Extreme Racing On Highway[/url]" = [url=https://assetstore.unity.com/packages/templates/packs/highway-racer-50866]Highway Racer[/url]
[*] "[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1058500]Muscle Car Robot[/url]" = [url=https://gamening.com/muscle-car-robot/]Muscle Car Robot[/url]
[*] "[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/809340]Extreme School Driving Simulator[/url]" = [url=https://assetstore.unity.com/packages/tools/physics/realistic-car-controller-16296]Realistic Car Controller[/url]
[*] "[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/645360]CubeXL[/url]" = [url=https://assetstore.unity.com/packages/templates/packs/switch-the-gravity-63196]Switch The Gravity[/url]
[*] "[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1058930]Top Burger[/url]" = [url=https://unityfreaks.com/asset/4815]Top Burger Chef[/url]
[*] "[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/628570]Trivia Night[/url]" = [url=https://assetstore.unity.com/packages/templates/systems/trivia-quiz-game-template-45521]Trivia Quiz Game Template[/url]
[*] "[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/864010]Space Force[/url]" = [url=https://assetstore.unity.com/packages/templates/x-racer-35344]X-Racer[/url]
[/list]

So the visuals might look halfway decent at first glance, if mismatched looking in places.  But that's only because the "developer" is using other people's assets.  When a dev is too lazy or untalented to make their own art, they usually aren't capable of competent coding or game design either. That is exactly the case with this mess.

Taking this shovelware seriously as if it was a genuine attempt to make a game, it doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.

One reason the "developer" chose to make this VR exclusive, apart from hoping VR compatibility would make an otherwise bad product somehow successful, might have been to prevent it being compared to non-VR games.

Developers must learn that while VR is great, if the only thing that makes the game great is the VR, then the game isn't great at all.

Making a multiplayer or PvP game VR-exclusive is a disastrous decision.  Steam's hardware survey shows less than 2% of Steam gamers have VR hardware, which means the developers deliberately eliminated 98% of their potential player base before the game even launched.  Multiplayer games need critical mass of players to survive, but the developer deliberately locked out 98% of the audience, then wondered why their game failed.

These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.

The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was [b]only 3 players[/b].  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 130 million gamers on Steam and well over 175,000+ games for gamers to choose from, the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected.

It's also important to note the "developer" here has connections to a number of shady Russian asset flippers and review manipulators who show an organised pattern to scam and defraud gamers with fake reviews and asset flipping the work of others for profit.  While reviews are about the games, gamers should be informed when developers act unethically.   Whether these connections are the same developer using multiple accounts, or just working closely with other unethical developers, gamers should be warned about the harm to gamers by this developer and their associates.  Buying games from unethical developers puts your money at risk.

This kind of asset flipping isn't harmless.  It makes it harder for gamers to find genuinely made games from ethical developers.  It makes it harder for genuine indie developers, who put hard work into trying to make real games, to find an audience for their products.  It gives indie developers a bad name.

Now on to pricing and value.  Should you buy this asset flip?  Is this really better than any of the 175,000+ genuinely made games on Steam?  Of course not!

Bocce Beach is relatively cheap at $5, but it's not worth it.  Remember that if you buy a game from an unethical developer, you're putting your money at risk.

Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, and the questionable ethical nature of the developer and/or their associates (as outlined above), this is impossible to recommend.
